h1: China S visa (S1 and S2): visiting family working in China

prices.included: Form completion, document check, visa centre appointment and submission support
Everything in Standard, with faster processing at the visa centre

intro: The China S visa is for family members of foreigners who work or study in China. The S2 visa covers visits of up to 180 days and the S1 visa covers stays of more than 180 days, for example a spouse or child moving to China with someone on a work permit. We complete your application, check your documents and book your visa centre appointment.
eligibility: The person you're visiting is a foreigner working or studying in China with a residence permit
For S1: you are their spouse, parent, child under 18 or parent-in-law
For S2: you are a close family member, or visiting for other private matters
If you are not British, you hold valid UK residence status

sections.heading: S1 or S2: which visa do you need?
sections.text: Choose the S2 visa for a family visit of up to 180 days. Choose the S1 visa if you're going to live in China with a family member who works or studies there for more than 180 days; after you arrive you apply for a residence permit within 30 days. If your relative is a Chinese citizen or permanent resident, you need the Q visa instead.

sections.heading: Do British citizens need an S visa?
sections.text: British passport holders can visit China visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 December 2026. You need an S2 visa if your visit is longer than 30 days, you travel on another passport, or you travel after the visa-free policy ends and it isn't extended. Family members moving to China need an S1 visa.

sections.heading: Documents for a China S visa
sections.text: You'll need an invitation letter from the person you're visiting, a copy of their passport and Chinese residence permit, and proof of your relationship, such as a marriage or birth certificate. For an S1 visa the relationship certificate usually has to be notarised and legalised, which our document legalisation team can arrange.

sections.heading: China visa help in Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and help travellers, families and businesses across the North West and the rest of the UK. Most China visa applications can be handled by post and email, so you only need to visit us if you want to. You can also collect your passport from our office at no extra cost.

title: China S Visa (S1 / S2) from the UK | Visit Family in China
description: China S1 and S2 visa help for UK residents visiting or joining family members who work or study in China. Documents, fees and how we help.

faqs.q: What's the difference between S1 and S2?
faqs.a: S2 is for short visits of up to 180 days. S1 is for close family members who will live in China for more than 180 days with someone who works or studies there.

faqs.q: Can my children join me on an S1 visa?
faqs.a: Yes, children under 18 of someone working or studying in China can apply for an S1 visa. We'll tell you exactly which birth certificates and legalised documents you need.

faqs.q: Do I need to attend the visa centre?
faqs.a: For a short stay (up to 180 days), usually not: until 31 December 2026 fingerprints are waived for short-term visas, so we can submit your application for you. Long-stay visas (stays over 180 days) still need fingerprints in person, and we book that appointment for you.

faqs.q: My relative is a Chinese citizen. Is the S visa right for me?
faqs.a: No, you need the Q visa (Q1 or Q2). The S visa is only for family of foreigners living in China.

documentsTable.details: Original passport, valid for at least six months with two blank visa pages, plus a copy of the photo page
Completed and checked by us before submission
Recent colour photo on a white background, meeting Chinese visa specifications
Signed by the person you're visiting, with your trip dates, the purpose of the visit and their address
Copy of the photo page of their passport and their Chinese residence permit
Marriage or birth certificate. For an S1 visa, notarised and legalised
Your UK visa or eVisa share code, if you are not British
Copies of any previous Chinese visas
